content.overview: BNS s. 145 — Habitual dealing in slaves.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Habitual dealing in slaves. BNS restatement of IPC 371. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 371. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 145 is the rule on “Habitual dealing in slaves”. The section provides that whoever habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 145 exists so that “Habitual dealing in slaves” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
145. Whoever habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
